createdBy: code review R7 (self-review; agent reviewers hit a session limit)
impact:
JS relational operators and Array.prototype.sort compare strings by UTF-16 code unit; Python's min/max/sorted compare by code point. The two disagree for every pair where one string has an astral character (>= U+10000, encoded as a surrogate pair starting at 0xD800) and the other has a BMP character above 0xD800.

Measured: for a = U+10000 and b = U+FFFD, Python says a > b; JS says a < b, because the lead surrogate 0xD800 sorts below 0xFFFD.

REACHABLE END-TO-END TODAY, at `src/aggregate.ts` first/last, which mirrors usage.py:186-187's min/max. Driving both implementations on an --instances payload whose project has two rows with dates U+10000 and U+FFFD:
  PY  last = U+10000
  TS  last = U+FFFD
Both exit 0. Different output, no error, no test or golden catches it. Realism is very low for a date field, so this is filed rather than treated as urgent.

WHY IT MATTERS MUCH MORE FOR T-004: usage.py calls sorted() in nine places (lines 394, 405, 429, 526, 574, 646, 650, 666, 684). Several sort by a numeric key, but ties fall back to insertion order and some sort strings directly. Project display names are derived from real filesystem paths and can contain astral characters — that is exactly the input class ISS-006 documents for encodePath. So every renderer T-004 adds is a new site for this divergence, and the failure mode is a silently reordered table rather than an error.

This is the FOURTH distinct defect from one root cause — JS counting/comparing UTF-16 code units where Python uses code points. The others: ISS-006 (encodePath missing the `u` flag), ISS-007 (padRight/padLeft padding by code units), and the splitCommand whitespace-class bug fixed in T-006 R6.

SUGGESTED RESOLUTION: treat this as a project-wide rule rather than three separate patches. Add a single comparator that orders by code point (e.g. compare [...a] against [...b], or use the fact that swapping surrogates for a code-point-ordered key restores Python's order), use it at every min/max/sort site, and add a CPython differential test over an astral/BMP corpus. Worth doing BEFORE T-004 writes the renderers, so the sorts are correct as written rather than retrofitted.

PRE-EXISTING and independent of T-006: the comparison operators predate this ticket and nothing T-006 changed affects reachability (an astral date passed validation before and after). Filed per the autonomous-session rule rather than fixed inline. Found by self-review in code review R7.
title: String ordering diverges from Python above U+FFFF (JS compares UTF-16 units, Python code points)
